findings.evidence: The compile test builds its own spine: an optional 'first' declare that closes before a sibling 'repeat' declare, with no occurrence div. append_sequence (pesuqei.py:129-153) produces something different: the repeat's False declare is nested inside the section-level True declare for the same feature, inside div#pesuqei_<stem>. So the critical case, an inner False overriding an outer True, is never compiled. The witnesses come from test_conditional_counterpart.doc, not witness_document, so the pb that retain_range_provenance inserts after the v16 marker never reaches the compiler. LinearData is built directly rather than from the frozen profiles. The frozen expanded spine already nests an override (qorbanot_barukh_shem_printing turns barukh_shem printed_translation false inside morning_printings, which sets it true), which suggests the semantics work. That is still not proof for this code.

findings.evidence: The check for exactly one guardable English provider only looks at this batch's generated documents. JLPTEI-3 lines 315-320: duplicate @corresp within a project keeps only the first indexed copy. If an existing file in the day-two English project (an earlier or later batch, or a shared library) already maps the target verse, refdb may pick that unguarded copy, and English would appear at the Hebrew-only repeat. Guidelines 92-93 and 375-379 require checking earlier and later callers and providers.
findings.action: In main, before writing, search every existing *.xml in project_directory/PROJECTS['en'] (except paths being regenerated) for milestone/@corresp == target and reject any match. Or, after the refdb refresh, assert there is exactly one en-project provider for each repeat target. Add a synthetic test with a pre-existing duplicate provider.

findings.evidence: The endpoint search skips containing-unit openers. Suppose a verse is followed in the same paragraph by the next chapter's opener (chapter milestone with @corresp) before any verse milestone. JLPTEI-3 rule 2 (line 182) ends the verse at that chapter, but the guard runs on to the next verse milestone. The result is a j:conditional that opens inside the resolved range and closes outside it, which is untested in the exporter. The text it covers is normally just milestones, so the risk is low.
findings.action: Stop at the earlier of the same-unit milestone and a containing-unit milestone that has @corresp, or reject when a containing-unit opener comes first. Add a test with a following chapter that has @corresp.

findings.evidence: Corrections run after guard_translation and after the provider-uniqueness check. A correction could remove or move the guard or its endConditional, or add a second English @corresp, and nothing re-checks afterwards. It is also not shown whether apply_corrections raises on a key it does not know (such as a spine path) or silently ignores it.
findings.action: After corrections, re-check that each repeat target has exactly one English milestone, immediately followed by its guard, with a matching endConditional before its same-unit endpoint. Confirm or enforce that corrections naming an unknown path fail.
